title: Join, or Die
creator: Benjamin Franklin
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: Benjamin Franklin, "Join, or Die," Pennsylvania Gazette, 1754. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: A segmented snake divided into eight labeled pieces representing the colonies, with the caption 'JOIN, or DIE.'

title: The Able Doctor, or America Swallowing the Bitter Draught
creator: Attributed to Paul Revere (after London Magazine engraving)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: "The Able Doctor, or America Swallowing the Bitter Draught," 1774. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: British ministers force tea down the throat of a woman (America) held down on the ground, symbolizing the Coercive Acts and Boston Port Act.

title: A Society of Patriotic Ladies, at Edenton in North Carolina
creator: Attributed to Philip Dawe (London mezzotint)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: Attributed to Philip Dawe, "A Society of Patriotic Ladies, at Edenton in North Carolina," 1775. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: British satirical mezzotint mocking American women signing a tea-boycott pledge at Edenton, ridiculing Patriot resistance.

title: The Horse America, throwing his Master
creator: Unknown (London print)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: "The Horse America, throwing his Master," 1779. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: A rearing horse labeled 'America' throws off its British rider (King George III) who wields a whip and cudgel, symbolizing the colonies' military resistance.

title: The Federal Edifice (The Federal Pillars)
creator: Massachusetts Centinel (Benjamin Russell)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: "The Federal Edifice," Massachusetts Centinel, 1788. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: A rising classical building supported by pillars, each labeled for a ratifying state, with a hand raising the next pillar into place.

title: The Providential Detection
creator: Unknown (Federalist print)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: "The Providential Detection," c. 1797–1800. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: An American eagle stops Thomas Jefferson from burning the Constitution on an altar to French radicalism, satirizing the emerging party divide.

title: Congressional Pugilists
creator: Unknown (American engraving)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: "Congressional Pugilists," 1798. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: Congressmen Matthew Lyon and Roger Griswold brawl with cane and fire tongs on the floor of the House of Representatives.

title: Mad Tom in a Rage
creator: Unknown (Federalist print)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: "Mad Tom in a Rage," c. 1801. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: Thomas Jefferson, aided by the devil, tries to pull down a pillar of the federal government, a Federalist attack tied to the election of 1800.

title: Ograbme, or The American Snapping Turtle (The Embargo)
creator: Attributed to Alexander Anderson
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: "Ograbme" (The Embargo), c. 1807. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: A snapping turtle labeled 'Ograbme' (Embargo spelled backward) bites a merchant trying to smuggle goods to a British ship.

title: A Boxing Match, or Another Bloody Nose for John Bull
creator: William Charles
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: William Charles, "A Boxing Match, or Another Bloody Nose for John Bull," 1813. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: President Madison and King George III as boxers; John Bull bleeds after a blow, celebrating a U.S. naval victory in the War of 1812.

title: Slavery As It Exists in America
creator: Unknown (American lithograph)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: "Slavery As It Exists in America," 1850. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: A pro-slavery cartoon contrasting an idealized scene of enslaved people in the American South with harsh Northern/British industrial labor.

title: The Propagation Society, More Free than Welcome
creator: Nathaniel Currier
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: Nathaniel Currier, "The Propagation Society, More Free than Welcome," 1855. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: A nativist cartoon showing the Pope and Catholic clergy landing in America, expressing fears about Irish and Catholic immigration.

title: The Age of Brass, or the Triumphs of Woman's Rights
creator: Currier & Ives
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: Currier & Ives, "The Age of Brass, or the Triumphs of Woman's Rights," 1869. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: A satirical cartoon of women voting and asserting rights while a man minds a baby, mocking the woman-suffrage movement.

title: Practical Illustration of the Fugitive Slave Law
creator: Edward Williams Clay (attributed)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: "Practical Illustration of the Fugitive Slave Law," 1851. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: Abolitionist William Lloyd Garrison defends a fugitive slave against a mounted slave catcher, dramatizing the abolition struggle.

title: A Foot-Race
creator: David Claypoole Johnston
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: David Claypoole Johnston, "A Foot-Race," 1824. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: Candidates Andrew Jackson, John Quincy Adams, and William Crawford race toward the presidency as onlookers wager on the 1824 election.

title: King Andrew the First
creator: Unknown (anti-Jackson Whig print)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: "King Andrew the First," c. 1833. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: Andrew Jackson stands as a crowned king in royal robes, trampling the Constitution and holding a veto, after vetoing the Bank of the United States.

title: The Way They Go to California
creator: Nathaniel Currier (Currier & Ives)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: Nathaniel Currier, "The Way They Go to California," 1849. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: Crowds of fortune-seekers scramble aboard overloaded ships and fanciful flying machines bound for the California gold fields.

title: Effects of the Fugitive-Slave-Law
creator: Theodor Kaufmann (lithograph, Hoff & Bloede)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: Theodor Kaufmann, "Effects of the Fugitive-Slave-Law," 1850. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: Armed slave catchers ambush and fire on a group of Black men in a field, condemning the Fugitive Slave Act of 1850.

title: Forcing Slavery Down the Throat of a Freesoiler
creator: John L. Magee
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: John L. Magee, "Forcing Slavery Down the Throat of a Freesoiler," 1856. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: Democratic leaders (Douglas, Pierce, Buchanan, Cass) hold down a giant Free-Soiler on the Democratic platform and force slavery into his mouth, over a burning Kansas.

title: The Political Quadrille, Music by Dred Scott
creator: Unknown (American lithograph)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: "The Political Quadrille, Music by Dred Scott," 1860. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: The four 1860 presidential candidates each dance with a partner while Dred Scott plays the fiddle at the center, mocking the fractured campaign.

title: Scott's Great Snake (The Anaconda Plan)
creator: J. B. Elliott of Cincinnati
repository: Library of Congress, Geography & Map Division
citation: J. B. Elliott, "Scott's Great Snake," Cincinnati, 1861. Library of Congress, Geography & Map Division. Public domain.
alt_text: A cartoon map showing a giant snake labeled 'Scott' coiling around the Southern states and blockading the coast and Mississippi River.

title: Emancipation
creator: Thomas Nast
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: Thomas Nast, "Emancipation," King & Baird / Harper's Weekly, 1863–1865. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: Thomas Nast's allegory contrasting the horrors of slavery with a hopeful future of freedom for African Americans after emancipation.

title: And Not This Man?
creator: Thomas Nast
repository: HarpWeek / Harper's Weekly (via Library of Congress)
citation: Thomas Nast, "Franchise. And Not This Man?" Harper's Weekly, August 5, 1865. Public domain.
alt_text: Columbia points to a wounded Black Union veteran on crutches and asks whether he should be denied the vote, arguing for Black suffrage.

title: Andrew Johnson's Reconstruction and How It Works
creator: Thomas Nast
repository: HarpWeek / Harper's Weekly (via Library of Congress)
citation: Thomas Nast, "Andrew Johnson's Reconstruction and How It Works," Harper's Weekly, September 1, 1866. Public domain.
alt_text: President Andrew Johnson portrayed as Iago beside a wounded Black veteran, blaming Johnson's lenient Reconstruction for postwar violence.

title: The Freedman's Bureau! An Agency to Keep the Negro in Idleness
creator: Unknown (Pennsylvania Democratic campaign broadside)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: "The Freedman's Bureau!" campaign broadside, Pennsylvania, 1866. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: A racist 1866 campaign cartoon caricaturing a Black man lounging while attacking the Freedmen's Bureau as wasteful to white taxpayers.

title: This Is a White Man's Government
creator: Thomas Nast
repository: HarpWeek / Harper's Weekly (via Library of Congress)
citation: Thomas Nast, "This Is a White Man's Government," Harper's Weekly, September 5, 1868. Public domain.
alt_text: An Irish rioter, a Ku Klux Klan member, and a Confederate (Nathan Bedford Forrest) clasp hands while trampling a Black Union veteran reaching for a ballot box.

title: The Man with the (Carpet) Bags
creator: Thomas Nast
repository: HarpWeek / Harper's Weekly (via Library of Congress)
citation: Thomas Nast, "The Man with the (Carpet) Bags," Harper's Weekly, 1872. Public domain.
alt_text: A traveler loaded down with carpetbags, satirizing the 'carpetbagger' figure of Reconstruction politics.

title: A Truce — Not a Compromise
creator: Thomas Nast
repository: HarpWeek / Harper's Weekly (via Library of Congress)
citation: Thomas Nast, "A Truce — Not a Compromise," Harper's Weekly, 1877. Public domain.
alt_text: A Union and a Confederate figure warily shake hands over a divide, commenting on the disputed 1876 election settlement.
